metadata.objective: Research and compile best naming conventions for AI agent knowledge repository

patterns: snake_case for all Python files and directories (crew.py, custom_tool.py)
Declarative YAML config separated from code (agents.yaml, tasks.yaml)
src/<project_name>/ nested structure
config/ subdirectory for agent/task definitions
tools/ subdirectory for custom tools
Single entry point: main.py
strengths: Clean separation of config (YAML) from implementation (Python)
Consistent snake_case throughout
Shallow directory depth (max 3 levels)
Descriptive filenames that match their purpose
weaknesses: No numeric ID system for tracking/referencing
No index.json or manifest for discovery

patterns: snake_case for Python directories (autogpt_platform/)
UPPERCASE for documentation (README.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md)
Dot-prefixed config files (.branchlet.json, .pre-commit-config.yaml)
classic/ vs autogpt_platform/ for versioned architecture separation
AGENTS.md for machine-readable agent instructions
strengths: AGENTS.md adoption for AI-readable project context
Clear separation of legacy (classic/) vs current platform code
Standard GitHub conventions for human-facing docs
weaknesses: Mixed naming styles across project evolution

patterns: snake_case for all Python modules
Monorepo with libs/ directory for sub-packages (langchain-core, langchain-community)
kebab-case for package names in monorepo
PascalCase for class names, snake_case for functions/files
Standard Python packaging (pyproject.toml, __init__.py)
strengths: Follows PEP 8 strictly
Monorepo structure scales well with many integrations
Clear package boundaries
weaknesses: No knowledge management or KB-style file organization

patterns: snake_case for files and directories
Role-based organization (roles/, actions/, tools/)
SOP-driven workflow encoded in code structure
Config files in YAML format
strengths: SOP-as-code approach aligns with this repo's coordination SOPs
Role-based directory organization maps to agent responsibilities
Clear input/output contracts between roles
weaknesses: Tightly coupled to software development domain

patterns: llms.txt at project root: lightweight summary with one-sentence descriptions
llms-full.txt: complete content with resolved specs
Markdown over HTML for AI consumption
Token-optimized structured text format
strengths: Purpose-built for LLM token efficiency
600+ websites adopted by mid-2025
Two-tier approach: summary index + full content
Adopted by Anthropic, Stripe, Cloudflare
weaknesses: Web-focused, not directly applicable to repo organization
No established standard for internal knowledge repos yet

patterns: AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md at repo root
Machine-readable project instructions for coding agents
Setup commands, testing workflows, coding style preferences
60,000+ public repos adopted this pattern by 2026
strengths: Industry-wide convergence on agent instruction files
Proven to improve agent task success by ~4 percentage points (developer-written files)
Low overhead to maintain
weaknesses: ETH Zurich study found LLM-generated context files reduce success in 5/8 settings
Comprehensive architecture-heavy files add 20-23% inference cost
Best when limited to non-inferable details only

patterns: Preferred terms vs variant terms for consistent indexing
Hierarchical taxonomy for categorization
Faceted classification (category + type + domain)
Metadata fields: some controlled-vocabulary, some free-text
strengths: Proven approach for large-scale knowledge retrieval
Reduces ambiguity in search and cross-referencing
Supports both human and machine consumers
weaknesses: Requires governance overhead to maintain vocabulary
Can be overly rigid for fast-evolving AI projects
Vocabulary maintenance is itself a task that must be automated

implicit_repo_rules.observed_pattern: KB-NNNN.md (zero-padded 4-digit numeric ID, Markdown with YAML frontmatter)
implicit_repo_rules.notes: Sequential IDs, no gaps except KB-0011 which is a placeholder. Title is in frontmatter, not filename. Category and tags in frontmatter.

implicit_repo_rules.observed_pattern: TEAM-NNNN.md (zero-padded 4-digit numeric ID, Markdown with YAML frontmatter)
implicit_repo_rules.compliance_rate: 93% (27/29 follow pattern; TEAM-0011 missing, TEAM-0026 present but no TEAM-0011)
implicit_repo_rules.notes: Matches KB entry IDs loosely (TEAM-0001 -> KB-0001) but not always (TEAM-0027 -> KB-0026). Some non-standard team files exist at teams/ root: TEAM-0022-comm, TEAM-0022-config.json, TEAM-0022-pipeline.py, SOPs.md, PROPOSAL-data-reform.md

implicit_repo_rules.observed_pattern: sop_NNN_descriptive_name.json (underscore-separated, 3-digit ID, snake_case description, JSON format)
implicit_repo_rules.compliance_rate: 85% (17/20 files follow; 3 non-SOP files in directory: efficiency_guide.json, future_team_data_strategy.json, tool_sops.json)
implicit_repo_rules.notes: Versioning via _v2 suffix (sop_012_monitoring_intervention_v2.json, sop_016_cross_team_data_flow_v2.json). IDs start at 011, not 001. Non-SOP files lack the sop_ prefix but sit in the same directory.

implicit_repo_rules.observed_pattern: SRC-NNNN-descriptive-name.json (UPPERCASE prefix, 4-digit ID, kebab-case description, JSON)
implicit_repo_rules.notes: Most consistent naming in the repo. Gap in sequence: SRC-0009 through SRC-0011 missing. Descriptive suffix is the API/service name in kebab-case.

Most inconsistent naming in the repo. Index uses kebab-case 'name' field but actual filenames vary. Some scripts have report files mixed in (stress-test-read-report.md, integrity-test-report.md). JavaScript visualization scripts use snake_case with viz_ prefix.
Most Python-conventional area. Prefix grouping: sdk_* for SDK-related, bus_* for message bus. No numeric IDs.

implicit_repo_rules.observed_pattern: TOOL-NNNN ID in index.json, actual paths are directories or single files
implicit_repo_rules.compliance_rate: 100% in index, but tool paths vary (sonnet-research-api/ dir vs doc_parser.py file)
implicit_repo_rules.notes: Directory names use kebab-case, Python files use snake_case. IDs in index but not in filenames.

implicit_repo_rules.observed_pattern: index.json at each directory level with version, count, and item array
implicit_repo_rules.compliance_rate: 100% (found in knowledge-base/, teams/sessions/, storage/scripts/, storage/sources/, storage/api-tools/, storage/coordination/sops/, market-research/picks/)
implicit_repo_rules.notes: All share common schema: {version, last_updated, items[]}. This is the repo's primary discovery mechanism. Consistent and well-maintained.

implicit_repo_rules.observed_pattern: TEMPLATE.md or TEMPLATE.json (UPPERCASE name, extension matches format)
implicit_repo_rules.notes: Consistent convention. Always at directory root alongside index.json.
Present in most top-level directories. CLAUDE.md at repo root serves as the primary agent instruction file.

implicit_repo_rules.observed_pattern: lowercase-single-word.md (no prefix, no ID, just topic name)
implicit_repo_rules.notes: Simplest naming in repo. No IDs or prefixes. ai-quant-techniques/ subdirectory also present.

best_practices.recommendation: Use snake_case for all filenames universally. Reserve kebab-case only for URL-facing paths or package names.
best_practices.rationale: snake_case is the dominant convention in Python/AI ecosystems (PEP 8), is used by all major AI frameworks (CrewAI, LangChain, MetaGPT), allows double-click selection of full names in most editors, and this repo's most consistent areas (coordination modules) already use it. The scripts directory's mixed kebab/snake is the repo's biggest naming inconsistency.
best_practices.token_impact: neutral (snake_case and kebab-case have identical token counts; consistency reduces cognitive tokens for agents parsing filenames)

best_practices.recommendation: Maintain the current PREFIX-NNNN pattern (KB-0001, SRC-0001, TEAM-0001, SOP-011, TOOL-0001) for all indexed resources. Standardize to 4-digit zero-padded IDs across all resource types.
best_practices.rationale: The PREFIX-NNNN pattern is the repo's strongest convention: 100% compliance in KB entries, sources, and teams. It enables unambiguous cross-referencing (builds_on: [KB-0001]), grep-ability, and sequential ordering. SOP IDs should migrate from 3-digit to 4-digit for consistency (SOP-0011 not SOP-011).
best_practices.token_impact: low (~2-4 extra tokens per reference for the prefix, but massive savings in disambiguation and search specificity)

best_practices.recommendation: For indexed resources, include the ID in the filename: {PREFIX}_{NNNN}_{short_descriptor}.{ext}. Example: kb_0001_storage_stress_test.md, sop_0011_commander_launch.json, src_0001_openalex.json
best_practices.rationale: Current KB and TEAM files use ID-only filenames (KB-0001.md) which require opening the file or consulting the index to know what they contain. Including a short descriptor (3-5 words max) in the filename enables faster discovery without loading file content. SOP files and SRC files already do this well. The descriptor should be max 32 chars and use the most discriminating terms.
best_practices.token_impact: moderate savings — agents can identify file relevance from ls output alone without reading file content, saving 200-2000 tokens per file that would otherwise need to be opened to check relevance

best_practices.recommendation: Maximum 3 levels of nesting from repo root. Current structure is already close to optimal. Flatten any paths deeper than 3 levels.
best_practices.rationale: Current deepest paths are 4 levels (storage/coordination/sops/sop_011... and storage/coordination/teams/a1-beta/output/). Research shows: (1) deeper nesting increases token cost for path strings, (2) AI agents struggle with navigation beyond 3 levels, (3) CrewAI and MetaGPT both cap at 3 levels. The coordination/ directory could be promoted to top-level to reduce depth.
best_practices.token_impact: saves 3-8 tokens per file reference by reducing path length; compounds across hundreds of references in a session

best_practices.recommendation: Use _v{N} suffix in filenames for superseded documents (sop_0012_monitoring_v2.json). Do NOT use version numbers for the current/active version — only add _v{N} when a new version supersedes. Track version history in the index.json, not in filenames.
best_practices.rationale: The repo already uses _v2 suffix in SOPs (sop_012_monitoring_intervention_v2.json). This is preferable to date-based versioning (which inflates filenames) or directory-based versioning (which increases depth). The current convention of keeping both v1 and v2 files is good for auditability but the index should clearly mark superseded status.
best_practices.token_impact: neutral for current version; adds 3 tokens per versioned reference but avoids the cost of version-directory nesting

best_practices.recommendation: Put in FILENAME: ID, short descriptor, version suffix. Put in FILE CONTENT: title, full description, date, author/team, category, tags, status, confidence, builds_on references, and all substantive content.
best_practices.rationale: Filenames should contain just enough metadata for an agent to decide whether to open the file (the 'index card' function). Everything else belongs in structured frontmatter (YAML for Markdown) or top-level fields (for JSON). This repo's YAML frontmatter in KB entries and TEAM logs is excellent — the pattern should be extended to all resource types.
best_practices.token_impact: high savings — agents can filter files by ls/glob without opening, then only read files they need; estimated 40-60% reduction in exploratory file reads

best_practices.recommendation: Continue the index.json convention at every directory containing indexed resources. Add a top-level manifest.json or llms.txt at repo root that lists all index files and provides a 1-line description of each directory.
best_practices.rationale: The index.json pattern is the repo's most successful convention (100% adoption, consistent schema). A root-level manifest would let agents discover the entire repo structure in a single read, reducing the multi-step directory traversal currently required. This aligns with the llms.txt two-tier approach (summary index -> detailed content).
best_practices.token_impact: very high savings — single-read repo discovery instead of recursive ls/glob; estimated 500-1500 tokens saved per new agent session

best_practices.recommendation: Use underscore (_) as the sole word separator in filenames. Use hyphen (-) only in ID prefixes (KB-0001) and kebab-case directory names that are already established. Never mix separators within a single filename.
best_practices.rationale: The repo currently mixes separators inconsistently: scripts use both (validate-storage.py vs grade_research.py), SOPs use underscore (sop_011_...), sources use hyphen in the descriptor (SRC-0001-openalex). Standardizing to underscore for word separation and hyphen only in the ID prefix (KB-0001) would create a clear, parseable pattern: {PREFIX}-{NNNN}_{descriptor}.{ext}.
best_practices.token_impact: neutral per-file but reduces parsing complexity for automated tools and agents

best_practices.recommendation: Formalize the existing implicit category vocabulary and enforce it via validation scripts. Current categories: methodology, integration, optimization, debugging, testing, tool-usage, market-research. Add: configuration, architecture, reference.
best_practices.rationale: The KB index already uses a fixed set of categories, but they emerged organically and are not documented as a controlled vocabulary. Formalizing them would enable automated categorization, reduce tag drift, and make cross-referencing more reliable. The existing validate-storage.py script could be extended to enforce the vocabulary.
best_practices.token_impact: moderate savings — consistent categories enable faster filtered searches; reduces false-positive file opens by 20-30%

best_practices.recommendation: Tags should be kebab-case, 1-3 words, from a curated but extensible vocabulary. Avoid tags that duplicate the category. Limit to 3-7 tags per entry. Add tag aliases to index for common synonyms.
best_practices.rationale: Current tags are already kebab-case and mostly well-formed, but some are redundant with categories (e.g., tag 'methodology' on a methodology-category entry), some are overly specific ('sop-improvements'), and some are inconsistent (both 'sops' and 'SOPs' appear in tags). A tag alias system would handle synonyms (e.g., 'multi-agent' = 'multi-team').
best_practices.token_impact: low direct savings; high indirect savings through more precise search results

best_practices.recommendation: Use JSON for structured data, machine-to-machine configs, and indexed resources. Use Markdown with YAML frontmatter for knowledge entries and logs (human-readable + machine-parseable). Avoid pure YAML files for complex nested data.
best_practices.rationale: The repo already follows this well: SOPs and sources are JSON (highly structured), KB entries and team logs are Markdown+YAML (narrative + metadata). JSON is 40-70% more token-expensive than equivalent CSV/compact formats, but the trade-off is worth it for the structured access patterns agents use. For tabular data specifically, consider CSV.
best_practices.token_impact: JSON costs ~40% more tokens than CSV for tabular data, but structured access patterns justify it for this repo's use cases

best_practices.recommendation: Keep filename descriptors to 3-5 words (15-30 characters). Use the most discriminating terms first. Abbreviate common terms (e.g., 'coord' for coordination, 'cfg' for configuration, 'proto' for prototype).
best_practices.rationale: SOP filenames are currently good length (sop_011_central_commander_launch = 5 words). SRC filenames are excellent (SRC-0001-openalex = 1 word descriptor). KB filenames are too short (KB-0001 = no descriptor). Aim for the sweet spot where an agent can determine relevance from the filename alone.
best_practices.token_impact: adds 2-5 tokens per filename but saves 200+ tokens per avoided file read; net positive for repos with 30+ files

key_findings: The repo has strong conventions in some areas (KB entries, sources, index.json pattern) but significant inconsistencies in others (scripts directory mixing kebab-case and snake_case, SOPs using 3-digit IDs while everything else uses 4-digit).
All major AI frameworks (CrewAI, LangChain, MetaGPT, AutoGPT) use snake_case for Python files — this repo should standardize on it.
The PREFIX-NNNN ID system is the repo's strongest pattern and should be extended to all resource types consistently with 4-digit zero-padding.
Index.json at each directory is an excellent discovery mechanism already at 100% adoption — adding a root manifest would complete the picture.
KB and TEAM filenames are too terse (just the ID, no descriptor) — adding a short descriptor would save agents hundreds of tokens per session by enabling filename-based filtering.
The llms.txt standard and AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md convention are converging as industry norms; this repo's CLAUDE.md is well-aligned.
JSON's token cost is 40-70% higher than compact formats but justified for this repo's structured access patterns.
ETH Zurich research shows that developer-written context files help but LLM-generated ones often hurt — keep CLAUDE.md focused on non-inferable details.
Maximum directory depth should be 3 levels; current storage/coordination/sops/ at 3 levels is at the limit.
